invariants: asset identity, history, minimum audit and outbox commit in one PostgreSQL transaction
tenant comes only from authenticated identity
human HTTP and gRPC upserts require stable idempotency identity, explicit reason and exact expected revision
Kafka binding replay identity derives from topic, partition, offset and item index before offset commit
direct binding identity includes tenant, MAC, IP, source and observed_at; missing tenant or observed_at is rejected
legacy discovery observations derive stable command identity from run and observation position and never append history outside the asset transaction
inactive lifecycle sweeps use a persistent daily request ledger and commit every changed revision, history, audit and outbox in one batch transaction
projection identifiers derive deterministically from tenant and asset identity
Kafka acceptance persists a verified inbox row before offset commit
OpenSearch and NebulaGraph advance independent idempotent watermarks without version regression
domain.compensation: rollback the PostgreSQL transaction before commit; after commit rebuild projections from outbox

negative_tests: cross-tenant body tenant is ignored and rejected on conflict

stop_conditions: transaction error rate or outbox lag exceeds approved budget

tests: G1 transaction fault injection including history/audit/outbox rollback
G2 real PostgreSQL including gRPC, binding, V1 discovery and inactive sweep
G4 upsert and sweep load profile
evidence: same trace_id across API, asset row, history, audit, outbox and projections

rollout.feature_flag: asset_discovery_jobs_v2 for the discovery-job cutover; atomic asset mutations are mandatory
